summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, chronic diastolic heart failure, and CKD stage 3, was admitted for recurrent syncope occurring while seated during a blood pressure check. The episode was consistent with neurocardiogenic syncope, similar to a recent prior event. His low heart rate on carvedilol was thought to contribute, so the dose was reduced from 12.5 mg BID to 6.25 mg BID and amlodipine increased to 10 mg daily to maintain blood pressure control. He remained stable without further syncopal episodes, was evaluated by cardiology, and discharged with a Zio patch for outpatient heart monitoring. His anemia remained stable on prednisone, folic acid, and B12, with a single unit of packed red blood cells given near discharge due to low hemoglobin. His CKD, diabetes, and cytopenias were managed without acute intervention. He was discharged home with services, under 24-hour supervision, and with follow-up planned in oncology, cardiology, and primary care.
